subject: LLM API handoff: discovery recap & compatibility next steps
messages:
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: samira.k@healthlytics.com; jordan.li@healthlytics.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: discovery call — migration off proprietary LLM APIs (next steps)

Samira / Jordan — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply with any corrections or gaps.

Key pain points you shared:
- Rising per-token costs on OpenAI for high-volume workflows (doc summarization, extraction).
- Latency variability across your production endpoints during batch inference windows (affects user-facing summaries).
- Auditability / data residency requirements for PHI-adjacent metadata (SOC2 in scope; customer data must remain in US).

Current stack (what I heard):
- Authoring + ingestion: internal ETL into GCS -> preprocessing on GKE.
- Model calls: mix of OpenAI (gpt-4o family) for chat & Anthropic (Claude-2/3) for long-form summarization.
- Orchestration: homegrown queue + retry logic; no KV caching today.

Success criteria for a migration pilot (suggested):
1) Parity on extractive QA and summary quality measured on your 30 prompt devset (target: within 5% of current rouge/precision metrics).
2) Sustained P95 latency <= 350ms for single-turn summarization under your 200rps pilot load.
3) Monthly token spend <= 60% of current OpenAI spend at pilot scale (after accounting for infra/infra-op costs).
4) Deployment within a US-only VPC with audit logs and KMS integration for model keys.

Redwood shortlists we discussed (initial):
- Mistral-Instruct-xxl (quantized variant) — high FLOPS efficiency, good for summarization.
- RedRock-2.1 (compatibility mode to Anthropic prompts) — potential for fewer prompt changes.
- Llama-3-Chat-XXL (8-bit quant) — strong for chat and instruction tuning.

Immediate next steps (timeline suggestion):
1) Tech deep-dive (1.5h) w/ your infra + our SEs to validate integration points and KV caching (week of Nov 29).
2) Provide a compatibility matrix + placeholder perf numbers (we attached a first-pass matrix).
3) Kickoff a 4-week pilot (sample size: 50k tokens/day) once procurement signs SOW.

Attachments: the email includes a stubbed compatibility_matrix.xlsx (first-pass model/latency/cost assumptions) and a draft SOW PDF for procurement.

Open questions for you (please confirm in reply):
- Are there any additional compliance requirements beyond SOC2 and US data residency?
- Can you share the 30-prompt devset we should use for the quality baseline, or do you want Redwood to produce a proxy set?
- Who is the procurement/contract contact for SOW review?

Thanks — I'll schedule the tech deep-dive tentatively unless you prefer to propose a time.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
Attachment: compatibility_matrix.xlsx (stubs: sheet "model_assumptions"), HealthLytics_SOW_draft.pdf (stub)

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthlytics.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 17:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery call — migration off proprietary LLM APIs (next steps)

Ben — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming a few clarifications and adding context: we want to keep a small Anthropic footprint for certain safety-critical summarizers for legal review (low-volume). Our primary motivation is cost predictability and latency consistency for user-facing summaries.

Clarifications / asks:
- Compliance: SOC2 + HIPAA parity for telemetry related to PHI (we're not storing PHI in the model, but logs may contain metadata). Can Redwood support HIPAA BAAs?
- Devset: we'll share a 30-prompt devset by EOD Tue (Nov 24) — cross-cutting docs with long-context and multi-section notes.
- Procurement: Jordan Li (copied on this thread) is the procurement lead — he prefers DocuSign for SOWs.

One more ask for the SE deep-dive: can you include expected delta on tokenization behavior (we get different token counts between OpenAI and Llama family) and example prompt adjustments for the shortlisted models?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Samira Khan
Head of AI Integrations | HealthLytics
samira.k@healthlytics.com | (617) 555-4821

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai; rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai; aditya.rao@redwood.ai; samira.k@healthlytics.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap: discovery call — HealthLytics (action for SEs)

Ben / team / Samira — looping Lauren in from SE to confirm items for the tech deep-dive. High level notes below and a proposed agenda for the 1.5h session.

Technical notes (preliminary):
- Tokenization: we see ~8–12% token delta between OpenAI gpt-4o tokens and Llama-3 tokenizers on your doc types; Mistral token counts tend to be 5–8% lower for the same content. We'll include concrete examples in the compatibility_matrix.xlsx.
- Latency: for an 8-bit quantized Llama-3-Chat-XXL we project P95 ~ 220–330ms on a single A100-style GPU with continuous batching; Mistral-Instruct-xxl (quant) sits slightly lower on cost but needs more prompt engineering for parity.
- Safety / Anthropic parity: we can keep a small Anthropic-sourced fallback for legal review flows; Redwood routing policies can send those requests to Anthropic while routing the remainder to on-prem/private variants.
- Compliance: Redwood supports HIPAA BAAs for Private deployments; we'll have legal looped if HealthLytics needs a formal BAA.

Proposed SE deep-dive agenda (90 minutes):
1) Intros & goals (5m)
2) HealthLytics architecture walk (10m) — Samira/Jordan
3) Tokenization & prompt delta examples (15m) — Rishi
4) Perf & cost projections per model (20m) — Lauren
5) KV/prefix caching integration and expected latency impact (15m) — Lauren
6) Compliance & deployment options (10m) — Ben/Rishi
7) Q&A and next steps (15m)

Next steps: I will take the compatibility matrix and produce a short appendix with tokenized examples before the call. Ben — please propose 2 time slots next week (Nov 30 or Dec 1) — we prefer morning PST.

Thanks — looking forward.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Attachment: compatibility_matrix.xlsx (updated: tokenization_examples tab)
